name: Preston

licensing.selective: No selective licensing in force. A scheme for City Centre, St Matthew's and Plungington wards, with a proposed fee of £1,050 per property for up to five years, was consulted on from 27 July 2026 into early October 2026; a decision is awaited.
licensing.additional: No additional HMO licensing scheme found; national mandatory HMO licensing (five or more people from two or more households) applies. An Article 4 direction restricting new HMOs was consulted on in early 2026 and, if confirmed, would take effect in February 2027.
licensing.fee: £1,050 per property proposed for the planned selective licence (£470 on application, £580 on grant)

housing: Preston's inner wards, such as Plungington, Deepdale, St Matthew's and Avenham, are dominated by Victorian terraces with a large private rented sector, many of them shared or let to students at the University of Central Lancashire. The city centre has a lot of purpose-built student housing and flats over shops. Fulwood and Ashton are more suburban, while the north-west of the city is growing fast with new-build estates at Cottam and beyond. The council is consulting on selective licensing in three inner wards.
checkinTips: Student lets in Plungington and near UCLan: photograph each bedroom lock, fire doors, alarms and the shared kitchen and bathroom separately.
Victorian terraces in Deepdale and St Matthew's: record damp at the base of walls, cellar heads, back yards and alley gates.
Georgian and Victorian houses split into flats in Avenham: note communal hallways, meter cupboards and the key count for each door.
Apartments at Preston Docks: note fob counts, parking bays and the condition of balconies.
New-build estates in north-west Preston: photograph snagging marks, sealant and the state of new turf and fences.
tenantHelp: Tenants can report disrepair, damp or unsafe conditions in privately rented homes to Preston City Council's environmental health team.
